born.sort: from the earliest born to the latest
born.shot: In what year was the composer {label} born?

rows.label: Ludwig van Beethoven
rows.hook: continued composing symphonies after losing his hearing completely

rows.label: Johann Sebastian Bach
rows.hook: filled churches with intricate fugues and cantatas as a working organist and choirmaster

rows.label: Frederick II of Prussia
rows.hook: played the flute and composed sonatas for his own court orchestra while ruling as king

rows.label: Pyotr Ilyich Tchaikovsky
rows.hook: composed the ballet scores for Swan Lake and The Nutcracker

rows.label: Sergei Rachmaninoff
rows.hook: composed sweeping piano concertos and toured widely as a virtuoso pianist

rows.label: Antonio Vivaldi
rows.hook: composed a famous set of violin concertos nicknamed after the four seasons

rows.label: Franz Schubert
rows.hook: wrote hundreds of songs and chamber works despite dying tragically young

rows.label: Gustav Mahler
rows.hook: composed sprawling symphonies while working as a renowned opera conductor

rows.label: Claude Debussy
rows.hook: pioneered a dreamy impressionist style evoking moonlight and the sea

rows.label: Antonín Dvořák
rows.hook: wrote a symphony inspired by his time living in America

rows.label: George Frideric Handel
rows.hook: composed a beloved oratorio whose finale is sung standing at Christmastime

rows.label: Johannes Brahms
rows.hook: wrote a famous lullaby and four symphonies in the Romantic tradition

rows.label: Igor Stravinsky
rows.hook: wrote a ballet score so radical it caused a riot at its Paris premiere

rows.label: Joseph Haydn
rows.hook: helped establish the classical symphony and string quartet as musical forms

rows.label: Edvard Grieg
rows.hook: composed the incidental music for a Norwegian play, including a famous mountain-hall march

rows.label: Maurice Ravel
rows.hook: composed a famously repetitive orchestral piece built on one steady rhythm

rows.label: Sergei Prokofiev
rows.description: Russian and Soviet pianist, composer and conductor (1891–1953)
rows.hook: composed a symphonic fairy tale where each character gets its own instrument

rows.label: Jean Sibelius
rows.hook: composed a stirring tone poem that became a symbol of his homeland's independence

rows.label: Niccolò Paganini
rows.hook: dazzled audiences with virtuoso violin skills so extreme some suspected a deal with the devil

rows.label: Gioachino Rossini
rows.hook: composed comic operas including one about a witty barber from Seville

rows.label: Nikolai Rimsky-Korsakov
rows.hook: composed an orchestral suite inspired by tales from the Arabian Nights
